title: Creating Animation Clips
description: Use the Animation window to record property changes and create reusable animation clips.

slides.title: The Animation Window 🎬
slides.content:
# Your Recording Studio

Open the **Animation** window (**Window → Animation → Animation**). Select a GameObject. You'll see a timeline.

To create a new clip:
1. Click the **Create** button and name the clip (e.g., "CubeSpin").
2. Unity automatically creates an Animation Clip asset and an Animator Controller (if the object didn't have one) with the clip assigned as the default state.
3. The window enters **Record mode** (red button).
4. Move, rotate, scale, or change any property in the Inspector – Unity records the changes at the current time.
5. Drag the playback head to a new time and modify again; keyframes are automatically created.
6. Click the record button again to stop.

quizData.question: How do you start recording a new animation clip?

options.text: Drag a clip onto the object
In the Animation window, click Create and then the red record button

quizData.explanation: The Animation window's Create button sets up the clip and enters record mode.

slides.title: Keyframes & Curves 📈
slides.content:
# Animating Properties

A **keyframe** is a snapshot of a property at a specific time. Unity interpolates between keyframes to create smooth motion.

- You can add keyframes manually by right‑clicking a property in the Inspector and selecting **Add Key**.
- In the Animation window, you see diamond‑shaped markers on the timeline for each keyframe.
- Switch to **Curves** view (button at bottom) to see and edit the interpolation curves (ease in/out, linear, etc.).

Common properties to animate: Transform Position/Rotation/Scale, Material color, Light intensity, etc.

quizData.question: A keyframe is a recorded value of a property at a specific point in time.
quizData.explanation: Yes, keyframes capture property states at time points.

slides.title: Sample Animation: Bouncing Cube 🟥
slides.content:
# A Step‑by‑Step Example

1. Select a Cube. Open Animation window. Click Create, name "Bounce".
2. At time 0:00, set position Y = 0 (Add Keyframe by clicking the record button or manually).
3. Move the timeline to 0:15 (15 frames). Set position Y = 3. Keyframe appears.
4. Move to 0:30, set Y = 0 again.
5. Stop recording.
6. The Cube will now smoothly move up and down when the animation plays.

You can also animate rotation to make it spin.

slides.title: Looping the Clip
slides.content: Select the animation clip in the Project window. In the Inspector, check **Loop Time** to make it repeat. You can also set **Loop Pose** and **Cycle Offset**.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Editing Keyframes

In the Animation window, you can drag keyframe diamonds to change timing, select multiple and scale them, or delete with Delete key. Right‑click for tangents (auto, free smooth, etc.).
